Subject: SLO synchronization & actionable probes — p95/p99 E2E targets

Alex / Ops team — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and clear next steps so we can get you a side-by-side verification of hosted vs your current provider. High level notes from the call: 

- Veridian target envelope: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 700ms (end-to-end, including network, gateway, and decoding).
- Expected steady-state traffic for initial proof: 120 qps sustained (text generation path), with short bursts to 400 qps for peak events.
- Streaming requirement: token-streaming to client with < 50ms per-token emission when in steady streaming mode; support for up to 60 concurrent streaming sessions per pod.
- Concurrency/slotting: average concurrency per user ~1.6; we should plan for request-level concurrency shaping and graceful tail fallback.

Attached a light probe spec and a mutual action plan. Concrete asks from us to you: 
1) Share a traffic sample (anonymized) for a 10-minute peak and 1-hour typical window (schema in traffic-sample.jsonl).
2) Confirm any egress/load-balancer path that adds >50ms to RTT (so we can model network delta).
3) Permission to run a hosted-side synthetic probe that mirrors your 1-hour traffic (we will use a dev namespace and tagged requests).

Our immediate next steps (from Redwood):
- Deliver an initial probe harness (nimbus-slo-harness link in doc) and run baseline against both hosted and an isolated instance of your incumbent (if you provide temp endpoints).
- Produce a p95/p99 comparison report with token-level breakdown and tail attribution (decode vs request queue vs infra).
- Recommend practical mitigations (batching window, KV cache hints, quantization profile) and an action plan for a 2-week pilot.

If the envelope above looks right, we’ll schedule the harness run early next week.

Thanks — Ben
--
Ben Carter
